papers.title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation increases slow waves during human NREM sleep
papers.summary: In 32 participants receiving 1 Hz transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) to the left insula/ventromedial prefrontal cortex during NREM sleep, tTIS increased slow-wave density by ~20% during and ~30% after stimulation versus a carrier-only control, with a stronger modeled field associated with greater shift toward N3 sleep. Source reconstruction and individualized field modeling showed waves involved more cortex without changed origins.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into state-dependent synchronization of neural activity by weak tACS fields
papers.summary: Simulating weak tACS in a detailed cortical column model across REM-like and NREM-like network states, stimulation entrained network activity at realistic field strengths despite minimal effects on firing rates. Entrainment was initiated by pyramidal cell entrainment recruiting interneurons state-dependently, with stronger locking in the NREM-like state, and recurrent connectivity was not required for or amplifying entrainment.

papers.title: Evidence for correlated evolution of sleep architecture in chronotype populations of Drosophila melanogaster created by artificial selection
papers.summary: Using artificially selected early and late eclosion chronotype populations of Drosophila melanogaster, the authors found correlated evolution of sleep architecture: early chronotype flies showed greater sleep fragmentation and shorter nighttime sleep latency, while late flies showed weaker changes. Environmental temperature cycles and light intensity modulated sleep timing, and recovery after sleep disruption and simulated jetlag differed between chronotypes.

papers.title: Cross-domain competition for memory reactivation resources during sleep
papers.summary: In a within-subject nap study with 24 participants, targeted memory reactivation cues for an object sequence task during NREM sleep did not indirectly enhance a linked motor task and disrupted object memory consolidation. EEG showed slow oscillation and spindle activity preferentially allocated to the motor trace, suggesting cross-domain memories sharing a common structure compete for reactivation resources.

papers.title: Cycle-based neurostimulation for control of circadian brain network dynamics in human epilepsy
papers.summary: Using longitudinal electrocorticography from individuals with bitemporal epilepsy, the authors found that alignment of circadian hippocampal connectivity rhythms between left and right hippocampus predicts seizure reduction to responsive neurostimulation, and stimulation timing predicts evolution of these rhythms. A nonlinear Kuramoto oscillator model showed in silico optimization of stimulation timing can improve predicted circadian network alignment.

papers.title: Integrating convolutional variational autoencoders and the Gaussian mixture model for efficient manifold learning and clustering of spatially preserved EEG topographic maps.
papers.summary: The authors designed Conv-VaDE, a convolutional variational deep embedding model that places a Gaussian mixture model prior on the latent space of a convolutional VAE with polarity-invariant mechanisms, for clustering EEG microstate topographic maps. Evaluated on 203 eyes-closed healthy participants from the LEMON dataset, Conv-VaDE showed highly reproducible latent geometry (silhouette 0.232 with narrow cross-subject IQR) and a modal K=4 in a rank-based meta-criterion (39.4% vs 29.6% for ModKMeans), while ModKMeans retained higher silhouette and 4-5 percentage points higher Global Explained Variance within the classical cluster-validity register.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.summary: This paper presents a BEM-FMM pipeline for EEG source localization using individualized 40-tissue high-resolution head models, computing TES solutions reciprocally to obtain leadfields at roughly 4.5 min per EEG channel on a single workstation. In six participants during photic driving, 40-tissue and 5-layer models produced highly consistent localizations (weighted relative difference below 3%), both closely agreeing with simultaneous MEG localizations in visual cortex.

papers.title: High-Density EEG Signatures of Cataplexy in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.summary: Using 128-channel EEG polysomnography in 10 drug-free adults with narcolepsy type 1 across 73 cataplexy epochs, the study found cataplexy exhibits a hybrid REM-like/wake-like spectral signature with mixed wake-, REM-, and N1-like hypnodensity probabilities. Signatures varied more between than within participants, supporting a dissociated hybrid brain state distinct from direct wake-to-REM transition.

papers.title: Preparatory beta activity reflects the precision demands of an upcoming movement
papers.summary: Healthy participants (n=27) prepared reaches toward narrow versus wide targets at the same location and timing while EEG and perturbation responses were recorded. Narrow targets yielded more precise movements with greater muscle co-activation and larger long-latency perturbation responses without reduced speed, and preparatory beta power (13-30 Hz) was lower for narrow than wide targets late in the delay over bilateral parieto-occipital electrodes, whereas alpha and theta did not differ.

papers.title: Heterogeneity of Sleep Complaints at Six Sites from 5 to 3,850 m in China: A Latent Class Analysis.
papers.summary: Using latent class analysis on PSQI and ISI data from 1236 personnel across six Chinese worksites at 5 to 3850 m, the study identified four sleep phenotypes graded by severity (no complaints 34.7%, mild 17.2%, moderate 33.5%, severe 14.6%; entropy 0.885) that recurred in all split-half samples. Chronic conditions were most consistently associated with disturbed classes (moderate aOR 2.48, severe aOR 3.49), habitual snoring with the severe class (aOR 2.00), and at 3850 m non-reporters of nocturnal oxygen use had slightly higher PSQI and ISI scores.

papers.title: BDNF-mediated amelioration of sleep disruption-induced behavioral disorders by Ginkgo biloba.
papers.summary: In a rat model of multiple-platform sleep disruption, intraperitoneal Ginkgo biloba extract (250 mg/kg) improved Barnes maze learning (probe-day latency 71±11 s to 38±8 s) and prevented the sleep-disruption-induced hippocampal BDNF decrease (381±17 to 557±27 pg/ml). Ginkgo biloba treatment also improved memory and reduced anxiety.

papers.title: A Neuro-Inspired Dual-Pathway Attention Network for EEG-Based Identity Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The authors proposed a neuro-inspired dual-pathway attention network for EEG-based identity recognition, separating a bottom-up perceptual extractor from a prior-guided top-down modulator fused by a quality-aware gate based on channel-wise and temporal variance. It reached 93.8% accuracy on DEAP (5.3 percentage points above the best baseline) and 97.2% on THU-EP, with only 2.5% and 5.2% drops in SEED-IV Sessions 2 and 3 and 76.8% accuracy using 1% of THU-EP training data.

papers.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 147 loci associated with obstructive sleep apnea
papers.summary: A large European-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis of obstructive sleep apnea (232,292 cases; 1,259,390 controls) identified 147 independent loci and estimated 16% SNP-based heritability, with six loci replicated in an African-ancestry meta-analysis. Gene enrichment implicated synaptic transmission (GABAergic and glutamatergic signaling) and cytoskeletal remodeling, and polygenic risk scores predicted OSA status, Fitbit-derived sleep features, and symptom-based risk across ancestries.

papers.title: Feature processing for single-trial semantic decoding from EEG: a factorial comparison with pre-registered replication
papers.summary: Across 640 feature configurations in three single-trial EEG semantic decoding tasks (40 participants each), signal representation had the largest effect: waveform-based decoding reached 56.6% balanced accuracy versus 50.6% for theta-band power (chance 50%), and adding band power to waveform reduced accuracy by 1.8 percentage points. These effects replicated and were larger in a pre-registered study of 283 new participants.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment enhances hepatic oxidative stress and antioxidant defenses without modulating immunometabolic gene expression in adult male mice.
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6 mice, six weeks of environmental enrichment lowered hepatic NAD⁺ and raised NADH, reduced lipid peroxidation and protein carbonylation, and increased antioxidant enzyme activities, GSH/GSSG ratio, and sulfhydryl content, while immunometabolic gene expression was unchanged. The findings suggest short-term enrichment optimizes hepatic redox balance without detectable transcriptional changes.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Profiles of Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Lines Harboring Circadian Clock Gene Mutations.
papers.summary: CRISPR/Cas9-engineered human embryonic stem cell lines carrying targeted truncations in CLOCK, BMAL1, NR1D1, and/or NR1D2 were generated with accompanying transcriptomic datasets, revealing genotype-specific transcriptomic alterations while largely preserving pluripotency gene expression. The resource supports investigation of non-canonical circadian clock functions in human pluripotent cells.

papers.title: Liraglutide Realigns Corneal Circadian Output Programs and Ameliorates Ocular Surface Abnormalities Under High-Fat-Diet-Induced Metabolic Stress.
papers.summary: In high-fat-diet-fed male C57BL/6J mice, HFD increased corneal rhythmic transcripts (2040 to 3582), delayed mean peak phase, and reduced phase coherence, while liraglutide shifted these toward normal-chow patterns and was associated with improved epithelial ZO-1/occludin, corneal nerve density, mechanical sensitivity, and reduced neutrophil and γδ T-cell accumulation. Canonical core-clock gene parameters showed comparatively limited changes.

papers.title: Preserved social development but impaired executive function in a Shank3 -deficient rat model of Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study transferred a targeted Shank3 mutation onto the Long-Evans rat strain and longitudinally assessed Shank3-deficient rats from infancy to adulthood. Despite profound loss of Shank3 protein, rats showed normal sensorimotor development and intact social preference, but adults displayed rapid error-prone responding in touchscreen discrimination and reversal learning, indicating executive dysfunction as a key consequence of Shank3 loss.

papers.title: EEG biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases: Machine learning applications and clinical trial insights.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from 226 studies on EEG-based machine learning and AI approaches for diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring, and patient stratification across neurodegenerative diseases. It reports that spectral power, event-related potentials, and connectivity are the main features with support vector machines and neural networks as primary classifiers, while highlighting persistent challenges of small samples and limited clinical validation.

papers.title: 'Therapeutic potential of resveratrol against REM sleep deprivation-induced memory deficits: involvement of hippocampal BDNF and TrkB protein expression.
papers.summary: In rats subjected to 6 h daily REM sleep deprivation for four days, resveratrol (40 mg/kg pre-treatment or 10–40 mg/kg post-treatment) attenuated fear-memory deficits (reduced freezing, increased freezing latency) and restored REM-SD-induced reductions in hippocampal BDNF and TrkB protein expression toward control levels.

papers.title: Circadian clock components CCA1 and LHY shape heat responses across regulatory layers
papers.summary: Using Arabidopsis circadian clock mutants with altered CCA1 and LHY expression, this study generated time-resolved transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data after short-term heat stress, finding that heat responses were dampened at both transcript and protein levels in cca1lhy and identifying CCA1/LHY-linked processes such as sulfur assimilation, ROS scavenging, and starch degradation as candidate contributors to time-of-day-specific thermotolerance.

papers.title: Circadian misalignment reshapes gut microbial rhythms to underlie digestive disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the bidirectional molecular architecture coordinating host circadian clocks and gut microbial rhythms—including feeding patterns, epithelial renewal, immune surveillance, bile acid metabolism, and rhythmic microbial metabolites—and discusses how circadian misalignment fragments microbial oscillations and increases susceptibility to inflammatory, metabolic, and malignant digestive disorders, with chronobiological interventions proposed to restore temporal alignment.

papers.title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of Alzheimer's disease through EEG normative modeling.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Using sex-specific normative models of hemispheric EEG small-world network architecture in 160 Alzheimer's disease, 161 mild cognitive impairment, and 769 healthy control participants, this study quantified individual deviations and identified two EEG-defined subtypes within both MCI and AD with distinct dysconnectivity patterns and cognitive profiles, including a higher-risk MCI subtype with widespread network disruption detectable before cerebral atrophy.

papers.title: Affective responses during five days of dexmedetomidine-assisted cold-sleep for long-duration spaceflight.
papers.summary: In a small study of six healthy volunteers (five receiving intervention) during a five-day dexmedetomidine-assisted cold-sleep protocol, mixed-effects modeling of daily PANAS scores showed no significant day effect for affective valence or arousal, and no major adverse affective outcomes or recovery rebound were observed.

papers.title: Novel Accelerated Heart Rate Index (AHRI) and cardiovascular morbidity: A retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 26,553 adults undergoing WatchPAT sleep studies, the novel Accelerated Heart Rate Index (AHRI) showed a U-shaped association with cardiovascular morbidity, with both the lowest and highest AHRI quartiles independently associated with higher risk (adjusted HRs 1.12 and 1.13). Associations were stronger in moderate-to-severe OSA and high hypoxic burden subgroups, and significant only for heart failure hospitalization among individual outcomes.

papers.title: Associations Between Indoor Musty Odors and Sleep Quality and Duration Among Older Adults: Longitudinal Study.
papers.summary: Using three waves of the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (5,712 older adults, 10,449 observations), indoor musty odors were associated with higher odds of fair and poor sleep quality and short sleep duration. These associations were significant among participants without chronic lung disease but not among those with it.

papers.title: An apparently de novo UBE3A missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) in the HECT domain in a child with an atypical early childhood phenotype suggestive of Angelman syndrome: a case report and focused literature review.
papers.summary: Case report of a 30-month-old boy with global developmental delay, severe expressive language impairment, EEG abnormalities, and delayed white-matter myelination, carrying an apparently de novo UBE3A HECT-domain missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The report provides a phenotype reference for future parent-of-origin and functional studies.

papers.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury following cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: integration of circadian rhythm and anesthetic factors to develop and validate a predictive model at 7 days.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 298 patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass developed and internally validated a nomogram predicting postoperative acute kidney injury (incidence 27.52%), incorporating circadian rhythm and anesthesia-related variables with an AUC of 0.796 in training and 0.776 in validation.

papers.title: A Nationally Representative Study of Complementary and Alternative Medicine Therapies in relation to Sleep Duration and Insomnia Symptoms among US Adults.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Using nationally representative 2012 NHIS data from 30,405 US adults, any complementary and alternative medicine use was associated with higher prevalence of short sleep duration (aPR 1.11) and insomnia symptoms (aPR 1.56), with the strongest insomnia association for meditation/guided imagery/progressive relaxation.

papers.title: Quality of life impairment in Parkinson's disease with probable REM sleep behavior disorder is primarily linked to fear of falling and anxiety.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cross-sectional study of 468 Parkinson's disease patients, probable REM sleep behavior disorder was associated with worse quality of life, but mediation analyses indicated this relationship was largely indirect, with fear of falling and anxiety accounting for much of it rather than pRBD acting as an independent predictor.

papers.title: Digital Phenotyping of Behavioral Instability as an Early Detection of Clinically Relevant Deterioration in Mental Health: Prospective Observational Multicenter Study.
papers.summary: A prospective multicenter observational study of 92 adults with mental health conditions used passively sensed smartphone data and Bayesian online change-point detection of behavioral instability to anticipate relapse events. The best model achieved a mean in-sample AUC of about 83%, with TPR of 40% at 5% FPR and 61% at 10% FPR, though performance varied across reruns and requires external validation.

papers.title: EEG and fNIRS evidence for brain responses to three tannins: implications for astringency surface sub-quality in red wine.
papers.summary: Using EEG, fNIRS, sensory analysis, LC-MS, and molecular docking, this study compared brain and sensory responses to three tannins standardized to equivalent astringency intensity in red wine. Iso-intensity tannins evoked distinct frontal cortical activation, with wine tannin producing the strongest neurophysiological and sensory responses, and higher tannin oligomer, polymeric pigment, and free anthocyanin levels were associated with finer astringency sub-quality.

papers.title: Standards to Support Healthy Sleep for Pediatric Inpatients and Their Families: A Delphi Survey.
authors: Sleep-Friendly Hospitals Task Force, on behalf of the International Pediatric Sleep Association (IPSA) Board of Directors
papers.summary: An International Pediatric Sleep Association Delphi study with 76 multiprofessional participants from 23 countries/regions developed consensus standards for promoting healthy sleep in pediatric inpatient care. The final output comprised 5 overarching standards with associated criteria covering sleep in the health care plan, senior management commitment, circadian rhythm promotion, family support, and environmental modification, achieving 96% agreement.

papers.title: 12-month trajectories of anxiety symptoms and functional recovery after new-onset stroke: A multicenter prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: This multicenter prospective cohort of 1934 patients with new-onset stroke used latent class growth modeling to identify anxiety symptom trajectories over 12 months. A high-increasing anxiety trajectory occurred in 20.5% of patients and was independently associated with poor 12-month functional recovery (adjusted OR 2.24), with most symptom change occurring in the first 3 months.

papers.title: Individualized Atypicality of Structure-Function Configuration Marks Subthreshold Depression in Adolescents
papers.summary: This study developed an isomorphic multimodal structure-function framework integrating five structural and five functional features to quantify individualized typicality of regional configurations in adolescents with subthreshold depression. StD participants showed lower typicality than healthy controls, with regional differences in frontoparietal and salience regions that aligned with PET and AHBA maps and correlated with depressive and sleep symptom scales, whereas conventional SC-FC coupling did not significantly differ.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea may exacerbate periodontitis via microbial dysbiosis: A preliminary translational exploratory study.
papers.summary: This translational study combined clinical 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics of gingival crevicular fluid in periodontitis patients with and without OSA with a rat model of chronic intermittent hypoxia plus ligature-induced periodontitis. OSA was associated with higher microbial richness, enrichment of Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium, glycerophospholipid-related metabolic differences, and, in rats, greater alveolar bone loss and inflammation, supporting a role for intermittent hypoxia and microbial dysbiosis in exacerbating periodontitis.

papers.title: Longitudinal ACC Alterations with Low-Dose Pregabalin in pBMS.
papers.summary: In a single-arm prospective longitudinal study of 38 moderate-to-severe primary burning mouth syndrome patients and 31 controls, low-dose pregabalin for 4 weeks reduced mean VAS by 3.28 points (ITT), with 44.74% achieving ≥50% pain relief. Baseline ACC Glx/Cr and tNAA/Cr were elevated and correlated with pain/sleep measures, and ACC Glx/Cr decreased after treatment alongside increased pgACC-centered connectivity, while gray matter deficits did not change.

papers.title: Wearable-measured 24-hour heart rate variability and neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a cross-sectional study
papers.summary: A cross-sectional All of Us analysis of Fitbit heart rate data found no significant association between sleeping heart rate and any AMD, but higher SDANN was associated with higher odds of neovascular AMD versus no AMD (OR 1.12 per 10 ms, Bonferroni-adjusted P=0.051). No associations were detected for epiretinal membrane or cataract, and the authors frame the finding as exploratory.

papers.title: Interrater agreement of seizure onset and spread in scalp EEG
papers.summary: Three board-certified epileptologists independently annotated onset and contralateral spread in 79 scalp EEG seizures from 48 presurgical patients, finding substantial agreement on onset laterality (Gwet k=0.73) and spread presence (0.63) but lower channel-level agreement for spread (Cohen k=0.38) than onset (0.57). Onset timing was more consistent (median MAD 0.40 s) than spread timing (1.99 s), supporting feasibility of scalp EEG spread as a noninvasive marker.

papers.title: Filgotinib Safety Profile: A Pharmacovigilance Study Using Data from the VigiBase and Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System.
papers.summary: A pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis of filgotinib using VigiBase (2207 reports) and FAERS (190 reports) from 2017 to 2025 identified strong signals for lower respiratory tract infection and hypercholesterolemia in VigiBase and for epididymitis and sleep apnea syndrome in FAERS, with median time to onset of 1 month. The findings support continued clinical vigilance for infections, metabolic abnormalities, and testicular-related adverse events.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
